title: Verity County Amateur Astronomers
description: Home page of the Verity County Amateur Astronomers, meeting monthly since 1978 and observing from Perrin Hill.

blocks.text: *** WELCOME TO THE V.C.A.A. HOME PAGE *** NEXT MEETING: SECOND TUESDAY, 7:00 PM, ROOM 104, COUNTY EXTENSION BUILDING *** NEW MEMBERS ALWAYS WELCOME, BRING A CHAIR ***

blocks.caption: The Verity County Amateur Astronomers -- Est. 1978

blocks.body:
[b]Welcome to our page![/b] This page is maintained by Dale Furniss (club president since 1996) on a Gateway computer in his basement, so please be patient if it is slow.

We are a small club. We have twenty six paid members and about nine who show up. We meet the second Tuesday of every month at 7:00 in Room 104 of the County Extension Building on Herron Road, and we observe from the [b]Perrin Hill gravel lot[/b] whenever the sky cooperates, which in this county is less often than any of us would like.

There is no dues increase this year. Dues are still $12, or $18 for a family, payable to Ann-Marie Tosches, who will remind you.

items: 10/14/2004 -- Added the October observing reports. Also fixed the link to the rail forum that Cliff has been emailing me about for a month. It is fixed, Cliff.
08/22/2003 -- THE POWER FAILURE. See the observing log. Best three nights any of us have had at Perrin Hill in twenty years and none of us are allowed to say we enjoyed it.
03/02/2003 -- New equipment page with the member scope list. If yours is wrong tell me at a meeting, not by email, I do not check the email.
11/09/2002 -- We joined the Gridfall Webring. See the bottom of this page.
06/17/2001 -- Page created. Thank you to Ben Tosches (age 15) for showing me how to do the tables.

blocks.body:
[b]OBSERVING SITE:[/b] Perrin Hill gravel lot, off Route 62 at about mile 15, north side, past the cattle gate. [u]KILL YOUR HEADLIGHTS AT THE GATE.[/u] Park facing out. Do not block the turnaround, the farmer uses it and he has been very good to us and we would like to keep it that way.

The lot is a quarter mile up the hill from where the radio people record, and we get along with them fine. If you see a car up there at midnight it is probably one of ours or one of theirs.

The single biggest thing hurting our sky is the sodium lighting on the county road and the security lights at the industrial park on the east side. We have been to the county board about this four times since 1994. Four times.

If you live in the county and you have a barn light or a dusk-to-dawn light, please put a shield on it. A shield costs about nine dollars and it puts the light on your property where you wanted it in the first place instead of into my telescope. That is the entire argument and it has never persuaded anyone.

The local paper printed a letter of mine about this in 1999 and the paper is at [url=synth://verityledger.com/]verityledger.com[/url] now if you want to see how little has changed. There is also a fairly good general write-up at [url=synth://wiki.gridfall.net/]wiki.gridfall.net[/url].

blocks.text: SEEING AND TRANSPARENCY ARE ESTIMATED, NOT MEASURED. IF YOU DISAGREE WITH A NUMBER, BRING YOUR OWN NUMBER.

blocks.body:
Entries are typed up from the clipboard that lives in the milk crate in my trunk. Seeing is 1 to 5, 5 is best. Transparency is the faintest star anybody could hold steadily at zenith, which is a crude method and we know it is a crude method.

Corrections are welcome [i]at a meeting[/i].

THE NIGHT OF THE SUBSTATION FIRE. See the note below this table.
Furniss, Jaris, Lane, Tosches x2, plus 6 visitors
Second night of the outage. Best sky recorded at this site in the life of this club.
Third night. Partial power back in Gridfall by then. You could see the difference from the hill, in real time, as the grid came back on.

blocks.body:
The substation on Gridfall Road burned on the evening of the 19th and most of the county was dark for three days.

I want to be careful about how I say this. People lost freezers full of food. The nursing home ran on a generator for two nights and that frightened a lot of families. A man on Ellery Street was hurt getting a generator down a set of stairs. None of that was worth anything to anybody.

And: from the top of Perrin Hill, on the 20th, five of us stood in a gravel lot and saw the Milky Way run from horizon to horizon with structure in it, and Wes held 6.3 at zenith twice, and Ann-Marie who has been doing this since 1988 sat down on the tailgate and did not say anything for about ten minutes.

Both of those things are true and I have never known how to put them in the same paragraph. That is the paragraph.

We had six visitors on the second night, people who drove up because there was nothing else to do with the power out. Two of them joined the club. One of them is Paul Lane's brother-in-law who now owns more equipment than the rest of us combined.

There is a good factual account of the fire at [url=synth://wiki.gridfall.net/]wiki.gridfall.net[/url], and camcorder footage of the aftermath at [url=synth://clipvault.tv/]clipvault.tv[/url] if you want to see what the morning looked like from the road.

blocks.text: WHAT WE ARE LOOKING AT NEXT

items: Double stars through the winter. Bring a list, do not just point at things.
The Jupiter opposition. Wes will bring the barlow he keeps promising us is worth it.
Anybody who wants to try sketching, Ann-Marie will show you. She is patient and you will be bad at it for a year.
The Messier list in one night, someday, if we ever get a March that cooperates. We have tried twice and failed twice.

blocks.body:
People ask at every meeting what everyone else is using, so here it is. This is not a competition and if it becomes one I will take the page down.

[b]If you are buying your first telescope[/b], talk to somebody in the club before you spend money. Every one of us has an expensive mistake in a closet. Ann-Marie has two.

blocks.body:
The club owns one 6 inch Dobsonian, donated by the estate of Harold Perrin in 1994, for whom the hill is not actually named (it is his family's hill, though, so close enough).

Any member in good standing may borrow it for a month. Sign the card in the crate. Bring it back with the eyepieces you took, all of them, both of them.

[quote=Ann-Marie, at the 2002 annual meeting]The loaner has been out eleven times and come back eleven times. That is a better record than the newsletter.[/quote]

blocks.caption: The loaner, in the extension building hallway, waiting for somebody to take it home.

blocks.body:
You do not need seven eyepieces. You need a low power one you trust, a medium one, and something for the moon and planets. Buy them one at a time, used if you can, and use each one for a season before you buy the next.

The man at the camera shop in Gridfall will sell you a barlow. You probably want the barlow. That is the one thing I will say in favor of buying something.

There is a long argument about all of this, with people shouting, at [url=synth://boards.gridfall.net/]boards.gridfall.net[/url], where there is a long argument about everything.

items: Collimate before you complain about the optics.
Let the tube cool for half an hour. Half an hour.
Dew heater or a hair dryer and an extension cord. Either works. One is cheaper.
Red flashlight. Red. Not a white flashlight with a piece of red cellophane falling off it, Paul.

blocks.body:
We get asked about this because our site is on Route 62 and because Wes is a member of both worlds.

There is a recording hobbyist who sets up about a quarter mile downhill from our lot and records shortwave. He publishes everything, including the nights with nothing on them, and he has been nothing but courteous to this club.

What we have seen from the hill: nothing. What we have heard: nothing. We are looking up, not listening, and we are usually busy. That is the whole of our contribution to the argument and we would prefer not to be drawn into it further.

His recordings are at [url=synth://clipvault.tv/]clipvault.tv[/url] if you want to make up your own mind.
